title: Odysseo Oceanarium
about_landmark_text: Mauritius's first and largest oceanarium, and the first in the Indian Ocean, opened on 6 September 2021 on the Port Louis waterfront. Spread across 5,500 square metres, it holds 2 million litres of water across 45 aquariums housing more than 200 marine species, arranged into six themed zones from mangroves to open ocean.
interesting_fact: The oceanarium's glass walls stand right beside the historic harbour that once welcomed the ships of early explorers - pairing a brand-new marine-conservation attraction with one of the oldest working parts of the city.

title: Port Louis Casino

puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: A casino at Caudan Waterfront, part of the complex that opened on 25 November 1996 on land once occupied by warehouses and a meteorological observatory. It occupies the Barkly Wharf building, named for Sir Henry Barkly, Governor of Mauritius from 1863 to 1870, and is known for a striking facade styled like the bow of a pirate ship, complete with bowsprit mast and statuary.
interesting_fact: The casino building's pirate-ship facade - a bowsprit mast and figurehead-style statues built into the architecture - makes it one of the more theatrical pieces of commercial design anywhere on the Port Louis waterfront.

title: SAJ Statue
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: A bronze statue of Sir Anerood Jugnauth ('SAJ'), unveiled at the Port Louis Waterfront on 15 June 2024, honouring the former Prime Minister and President who dominated Mauritian politics for decades. It stands beside an earlier statue of Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam, placing two of independent Mauritius's most prominent leaders side by side on the same esplanade.
interesting_fact: At 3.6 metres tall, the SAJ statue was built about 30 centimetres taller than the neighbouring Ramgoolam statue, and its Rs 13.5 million cost and sculptor Devanand Bungshee's likeness both drew public criticism at the time of unveiling.

title: Aapravasi Ghat World Heritage Site
clue_text: PLACEHOLDER - walk to Aapravasi Ghat World Heritage Site.
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2006, and the place where the modern indentured-labour diaspora began. Built in 1849, the Aapravasi Ghat ("Immigration Depot") was the main entry point for almost 500,000 indentured labourers - mostly from India, but also China, Africa, Madagascar and Southeast Asia - brought to Mauritius between 1849 and 1923, mainly to work the island's sugar plantations after the abolition of slavery.
interesting_fact: Roughly 70% of Mauritians today are descended from these indentured labourers - making this small 1,640 m² depot one of the most significant sites anywhere for understanding the origins of modern Mauritian society, and one of the earliest examples of the labour-migration system that would go on to reshape economies worldwide.

title: China Town South Gate
clue_text: PLACEHOLDER - walk to China Town South Gate.
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: One of the ornamental Friendship Gates marking the entrance to Port Louis's Chinatown on Royal Road, one of the oldest Chinatowns in Africa. The gates were a gift from Foshan, in Guangdong province, Port Louis's twin city in China, symbolising the long-standing links between the two places and the wider friendship between Mauritius and China.
interesting_fact: Chinatown's roots reach back to the 1780s, when the first Chinese migrants arrived in Port Louis from Guangzhou aboard British, French and Danish ships - making it one of the oldest continuously inhabited Chinese communities anywhere in Africa.

title: Manga Street Murals
address: Venpin Street, off Royal Road, Chinatown, Port Louis, Mauritius
clue_text: PLACEHOLDER - walk to Manga Street Murals.
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: Duck into the narrow passage off Royal Road that everyone in Chinatown just calls Manga Street, and the walls close in with colour - a girl with sea-green hair, a blue-haired swordsman mid-strike, a golden-haired heroine wreathed in mist, each panel painted floor to roof on old shopfront brick. Every figure here was put up for free in June 2020 by young volunteer artists working with the New Chinatown Foundation, on a stretch of Venpin Street that had sat abandoned for years - proof, as one of the organisers put it at the time, that young people still show up to volunteer for their own neighbourhood.
interesting_fact: Many of the murals were painted to mark the 50th anniversary of diplomatic ties between Mauritius and China, turning a once-derelict back alley into one of the most photographed corners of Port Louis.

title: Jummah Masjid
address: Royal Road, Queen St, Port Louis, Mauritius
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: Port Louis's principal mosque, on Royal Road in the heart of the old commercial quarter. Members of the city's mercantile community bought the site on Queen Street in 1852 and consecrated the mosque in 1853, when it was known as the "Mosque of the Arabs." A major expansion begun in 1878, overseen by Jackaria Jan Mahomed, was delayed for years by disease and construction-supply shortages and wasn't finished until 1895 - the building seen today is largely that late-19th-century enlargement.
interesting_fact: The mosque blends Indian, Creole and Islamic architectural styles, and is widely described as one of the most beautiful religious buildings in Mauritius. A marble tomb beside the mosque holds the remains of Jamal Shah, a pir (Sufi holy man) from Kutch in India.

title: Central Market Port Louis
clue_text: PLACEHOLDER - walk to Central Market Port Louis.
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: The historic heart of Port Louis's daily life, dating to 1839 under British colonial rule (the market itself traces back further, to a 1828 origin before moving to this site in 1833). Its wrought-iron gates, decorated with floral motifs and dating from 1839, are a well-known piece of the city's Victorian-era heritage. The building was heavily renovated between 2001 and 2004 after several fires, while its original character was preserved.
interesting_fact: For nearly two centuries the market has been a meeting point for all of Mauritius's communities - Creole, Franco-Mauritian, Indian, Chinese and African - trading side by side, and it's still often called the Bazaar or Victoria Market by locals.

title: Statue of William Newton
clue_text: PLACEHOLDER - walk to Statue of William Newton.
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: A statue of Sir William Newton (1842-1915), a Mauritian lawyer of mixed Indo-Mauritian and Scottish descent who led the reformist movement launched in 1882 demanding an elected element in the colonial Legislative Council. His campaigning under the administration of Governor Sir John Pope Hennessy helped bring about the Constitutional Reform of 1885, which for the first time let Indo-Mauritians and other non-white islanders elect their own representatives.
interesting_fact: The Constitution Newton helped win came into force on 20 October 1885 - the first time in Mauritian history that non-white islanders could vote for their own representatives in the colonial legislature.

title: Port Louis Theatre
address: Remy Ollier St & Jules Koenig St, Port Louis, Mauritius
clue_text: PLACEHOLDER - walk to Port Louis Theatre.
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: The Port Louis Theatre, the oldest theatre in the Indian Ocean region. Governor Robert Farquhar laid its first stone in 1820, and architect Pierre Poujade built it in the style of classic London playhouses, with the theatre inaugurated on 11 June 1822. Inside, three tiers of seating for around 600 sit beneath an ornately painted dome ceiling of cherubs and chandeliers, and for over a century it was the island's sole home for opera, drama and balls, until the Plaza Theatre opened in Rose Hill in 1933.
interesting_fact: The idea of bringing theatre to Mauritius dates back even earlier than the building itself - a French warship's health officer first brought a troupe to perform in Port Louis in 1790, though it was disbanded just two years later by a smallpox epidemic.

title: Statue de Saint Louis
address: St. Louis Cathedral's Garden, Pope Hennessy St, Port Louis, Mauritius
clue_text: PLACEHOLDER - walk to Statue de Saint Louis.
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: A statue of Saint Louis (King Louis IX of France) standing in the garden of St Louis Cathedral, honouring the city and cathedral's namesake saint. It provides a quiet, reflective spot in the cathedral grounds, framed by the church's striking facade and well-kept gardens in the heart of Port Louis.

title: Photographic Museum Of Mauritius
address: Rue du Vieux Conseil, Port Louis, Mauritius
clue_text: PLACEHOLDER - walk to Photographic Museum Of Mauritius.
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: A museum of historic photography on Rue du Vieux Conseil, founded in 1966 by photographer Tristan Bréville and his wife to preserve the island's photographic memory since 1839. Housed in an 18th-century building that once belonged to French botanist and administrator Pierre Poivre, it holds over 50,000 old photographs of Mauritius along with a collection of historic cameras and equipment.
interesting_fact: Among its collection is one of the rarest lenses in photographic history, made by Charles Chevalier for Jacques Daguerre - inventor of the daguerreotype - in 1834, just a few years before photography itself was publicly unveiled.

title: Natural History Museum
clue_text: PLACEHOLDER - walk to Natural History Museum.
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: The Mauritius Institute's Natural History Museum, on the ground floor of a National Heritage building constructed between 1880 and 1884 and modelled partly on Sri Lanka's Colombo Museum. Its collections trace back to 1826, when naturalists Julien Desjardins and Louis Bouton first proposed a museum to the governor - the resulting Desjardins Museum opened in 1842, decades before the current building existed, and the institution was declared a National Museum in 2000.
interesting_fact: The museum's most complete dodo skeleton was not unearthed until 1904, discovered by a Port Louis barber named Étienne Thirioux, whose amateur fossil-hunting turned up one of the best specimens of the extinct bird ever found.

title: Bust of Queen Victoria
clue_text: PLACEHOLDER - walk to Bust of Queen Victoria.
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: A bust of Queen Victoria near the Port Louis waterfront, distinct from the full-length Queen Victoria Statue that stands at Place d'Armes in front of Government House (erected 1897). Like that statue, it dates from an era when such colonial-era tributes to the monarch were common across British territories.

title: Caudan Arts Centre
clue_text: PLACEHOLDER - walk to Caudan Arts Centre.
puzzle_question: PLACEHOLDER - what is this landmark called?
about_landmark_text: A performing-arts venue at Caudan Waterfront built on what was once a car park, inaugurated in December 2018 as the first new theatre built in Mauritius in nearly a century. Its 431-seat auditorium, designed by architect Maurice Giraud and Didier Ho Architecture with acoustics engineering by Arup, hosts drama, music and dance, alongside a restaurant, bars, a conference room and exhibition space.
interesting_fact: Before this venue opened in 2018, Mauritius had gone almost 100 years without a purpose-built theatre - making the Caudan Arts Centre the first new stage of its kind on the island in nearly a century.
